summary: Verified the Railway PostgreSQL workflow foundation and upgraded the governed supportive-outreach artifact to a reproducible 12,000-case longitudinal synthetic cohort with structured missingness, temporal shift validation, calibration gates, and Python-to-TypeScript parity.

commands: PostgreSQL 17 scratch cluster: apply database/migrations/*.sql in timestamp order and run psql -f tests/database/launch_workflow.sql
tests.notes: Database evidence remains current: six migration tests and the PostgreSQL 17 transactional suite passed. The v2 artifact regenerated exactly from 12,000 synthetic encounters across 6,000 patient-disjoint identities; seven ML tests, two focused TypeScript runtime parity/fail-closed tests, and all 33 broader server/contract/FHIR tests passed. The 2,400-case future holdout achieved ROC AUC 0.7024, Brier 0.1657, log loss 0.5055, and expected calibration error 0.0163; every reviewed cadence, barrier, missingness, profile, and future-window subgroup passed. No public, restricted, or real patient dataset was downloaded or committed.

notes_for_next_agent: Apply database/migrations/*.sql in timestamp order through the Railway release/pre-deploy migration runner using only the API service's private DATABASE_URL; these migrations contain no environment URL or credential.

The in-process API poller should call try_scheduler_lock(scenario_id) inside its claim transaction, then use claim_scheduled_actions and claim_outbox with bounded limits. PostgreSQL due times, claims, and leases remain scheduler authority.

recover_stale_claims makes unattempted expired work retryable but converts any possibly accepted provider send to outcome_unknown and marks its provider attempt reconciliation_required. Do not retry that action until provider identity, signed callback, or manual recovery establishes the outcome.

The fixed finals scenario UUID remains 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. reset_finals_scenario() restores fixed seed state and the inert T-3/T-1 schedule without leaving outbox, provider-attempt, or webhook effects.

The Railway connection role owns runtime least-privilege configuration. Platform-specific client roles, extension-based schedulers, secret stores, and database-owned HTTP scheduling are not part of this target.

The runtime artifact path remains artifacts/ml/supportive-outreach-v1 while model_version advances to supportive-outreach-2.0.0; the feature schema and portable format remain compatible with the fail-closed TypeScript loader.

ml/MODEL_CARD.md records the official public-source review and why adjacent access, communication, screening, adherence, and intervention datasets cannot truthfully supply the exact pre-treatment supportive-outreach-acceptance target.
